transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, thanks. Um… I guess I’m here because I’ve been kind of arranging my days around avoiding certain drives—mostly those really high bridges. It’s probably not the biggest thing, but it’s gotten inconvenient. If I can’t avoid one, I can get through it, I just… grip the wheel pretty hard and feel tense the whole way.
Do you feel this kind of fear only when driving over high bridges?

Mostly, yeah. I mean, not every little bridge or anything. It’s really those high ones over the bay. I know they’re built fine, and people drive over them all day, so I feel kind of silly saying it… but when I get near one, my mind goes right to, like, the car could somehow go over the side.
Outside of high bridges, do you often find yourself worrying a lot about many other parts of everyday life?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I worry about normal stuff like anyone does, work or bills here and there, but I wouldn’t say it’s a lot of different things every day. It’s really more that bridge situation. Does that make sense?
Do you get this same kind of fear in other places where it might feel hard to get away?
I don’t think so, no. I’m trying to think… like elevators or crowded places, that sort of thing? Those don’t really bother me in the same way. It’s more the high bridge part, if that’s what you mean.
If you were a passenger—not the driver—going over a high bridge, would you still feel afraid?

Yeah… I think I would still feel it, honestly. Maybe a little less if someone else was driving, but when we get near one of those high bridges over the bay, my mind still goes to that same place—like, even though I know it’s safe and people cross it all day, I picture the car somehow going over the side. I know that probably sounds kind of unreasonable.
